songInfo.title: Basket Case
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Ionian Pachelbel Progression in Punk Rock

scalesUsed.notes: Eb - F - G - Ab - Bb - C - D
scalesUsed.application: The diatonic framework for the Pachelbel Canon progression
Melodic vocal hooks and high-energy power chord roots

mainProgression.progression: I - V - vi - iii - IV - I - V (Pachelbel Canon)
mainProgression.description: The classical Pachelbel Canon harmonic progression supercharged into 175 BPM pop-punk adrenaline

sectionProgressions.progression: Eb5 - Bb5 - C5 - G5 - Ab5 - Eb5 - Bb5
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - V - vi - iii - IV - I - V
sectionProgressions.description: Muted palm-picking building tension before explosive drums enter

sectionProgressions.progression: Ab5 - Bb5 - Eb5 - C5 - Ab5 - Bb5 - Eb5
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: IV - V - I - vi - IV - V - I
sectionProgressions.description: Anthemic release hook ('Sometimes I give myself the creeps')
Rapid cyclical drive leading into the final triumphant chorus

harmonicFunction: Pachelbel Canon progression (I-V-vi-iii-IV-I-IV-V) provides instant classical familiarity and melodic forward momentum
Root-5 and Root-6 power chords allow lightning-fast fretboard position shifts at 175 BPM
The chorus pivots to IV (Ab5) for dramatic dynamic explosion and emotional release
Half-step down tuning adds extra low-end resonance and gives standard barre chord grips a darker, punchier crunch

techniques.name: High-Speed Palm-Muted Power Chords
techniques.description: Executing precise, aggressive downstrokes at 175 BPM with right-hand palm muting

notes: Billie Joe Armstrong's signature right-hand rhythm technique
Lightly rest the fleshy edge of the picking palm against the bridge saddles
Keep the downstroke attack completely consistent in dynamic volume and punch
sequence: Release palm mute for open explosive accents on chorus transitions
tips: Use wrist motion rather than the entire forearm to prevent fatigue at 175 BPM
Use a heavy pick (0.88mm to 1.0mm) for maximum percussive definition

techniques.name: Rapid Position Shifting
techniques.description: Jumping cleanly between 5th-string and 6th-string power chord grips across the fretboard

notes: Eb5 (6th fret string 5) to Bb5 (6th fret string 6) to C5 (8th fret string 5)
Keep fretting fingers locked in the 2-finger power chord clamp
Slide smoothly without lifting hand off the strings
sequence: Hop index finger up one string to 6th string root
tips: Mute unused strings with the underside of your fretting index finger
Look at the target fret before shifting your fretting hand

sections.name: Intro (Clean/Solo Guitar)
sections.description: Billie Joe Armstrong alone with electric guitar singing 'Do you have the time to listen to me whine?'.
sections.progression: Eb5 - Bb5 - C5 - G5 - Ab5 - Eb5 - Bb5
notes: Palm mute lightly for punchy, percussive definition
Open up strumming dynamics as the drums slam in

sections.name: Full Band Verse
sections.description: The full band explodes into the driving verse groove with Tre Cool's pounding drums and Mike Dirnt's bass.
sections.progression: I - V - vi - iii - IV - I - V
notes: Keep right hand loose to sustain 175 BPM energy
Punch the accents on the snare hits

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: 'Sometimes I give myself the creeps... sometimes my mind plays tricks on me' arena hook.
sections.progression: Ab5 - Bb5 - Eb5 - C5 - Ab5 - Bb5 - Eb5
notes: Quick syncopated hits on the transitions
Sustained final Eb5 leading into the post-chorus riff

guitar.recommended: Fernandes Stratocaster 'Blue' copy with angled bridge humbucker
guitar.pickup: Seymour Duncan JB (SH-4) bridge humbucker mounted at an angle

amp.recommended: Marshall 1959 Super Lead 100W ('Pete' modded head with high gain)

effects.distortion: Pure cranked Marshall tube overdrive with punchy midrange bite
effects.reverb: Dry studio room sound with minimal reverb for tight punch

beginner.title: Pachelbel Power Chord Sequence
steps: Tune guitar down a half-step to Eb Standard
Learn the 2-finger power chord shape for Eb5, Bb5, C5, G5, Ab5
Practice the sequence at 100 BPM with downstrokes

intermediate.title: Palm Muting & Stamina Building
steps: Master the palm-muting technique on the low strings
Build right-hand wrist stamina from 120 BPM up to 175 BPM
Seamlessly transition between palm-muted verse and explosive chorus

advanced.title: Full Speed Performance & Vocals
steps: Play the entire song from start to finish without right-hand fatigue
Synchronize rapid downstrokes while singing lead vocals
Lock tightly into the drum groove on the syncopated chord stops

commonMistakes: Tensing the entire arm at 175 BPM, leading to exhaustion within 30 seconds
Failing to mute the open strings causing muddy discordance between power chord jumps
Skipping the G5 chord in the Pachelbel sequence
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Wrist stretching and chromatic downstroke warm-up
10 min: Power chord position shift accuracy drills at 120 BPM
15 min: Metronome stamina drills increasing from 140 to 175 BPM
10 min: Full playthrough with Dookie album track
focusAreas: Fretting hand precision on Root-5 to Root-6 shifts
Relaxed picking wrist mechanics at high tempo
Dynamic contrast between palm-muted verse and open chorus
metronomeWork: Start metronome at 120 BPM with steady eighth-note clicks
Bump tempo by 5 BPM increments once you can play 4 cycles without error
Target steady, clean execution at album speed of 175 BPM
